name: Wasteland Exploration
summary: The Wasteland Exploration chart, for Marienburg and the moors, marshes and coast around it. It replaces the rulebook's chart. The five-of-a-kind results are exclusive Marienburg locations: only one warband can hold each type of encampment, and if another player rolls the same result the encampment is contested in the next round by playing Scenario 10: The Sting.
income_note: The dice total gives the number of treasures secured, sold by the rules for selling wyrdstone. Then roll a D6 for each piece of treasure: on a 6 it is warp-tainted and counts as a wyrdstone shard, which can be taken to the alchemist as a shard is. Players are encouraged to use whichever currency suits their warband.

places.name: Stagnant Pool
places.rules: Nominate one of the Heroes in the warband to scout the wetlands. He must pass an Initiative test. If he fails he is dragged to his death by quicksand. If he passes, each warrior in the warband takes a Strength 1 hit from mosquito bites; Undead and daemons are immune to insects. If the Hero passes the Initiative test, roll on the Herbs & Potions Chart (see Herbalist in the Marketplace).

places.name: Marine Grotto
places.rules:
Roll a D6 for each entry:
D3 Nets 2+
2D6 gold crowns 3+
Trident 4+
Jewel Necklace 5+
Chest (roll a D6 on the Cargo Chart) 6+
The Jewel Necklace can be worn by a Hero in the warband: he gains +1 to the rolls for locating rare items. Roll on the Cargo Chart to see what the chest contains.

places.name: Orphanage
places.rules:
Witch Hunters visiting the orphanage search the premises. If the leader passes a Leadership test they find mutants in the basement: distribute D3 Experience amongst the Heroes in the warband.
If the orphanage is visited by a Skaven or Goblin warband, or a warband following the plot 'The Body Trade', they capture one of the orphans. Add the orphan captive as a hostage to the warband's roster sheet for stored equipment.
If it is visited by followers of Chaos they capture one of the mutant children instead. Add the mutant to the warband's roster sheet; this counts towards the plot achievement for 'Gaze of the Gods'. If the warband returns to the orphanage they capture one of the orphans, added as a hostage to stored equipment on the roster sheet.
Any other warband makes a donation of D6 gold crowns and receives the blessings of Shallya: any model may immediately recover 1 Wound in the next battle.

places.name: Whiskey Distillery
places.rules: Two Heroes from the warband visit the makeshift brewery. Roll once on the Drinking Chart for the Gentleman's Club from Infamous Haunts. The Heroes walk out with a barrel unless one of them is placed under arrest. Roll on the Cargo Chart to see what the barrel contains.

places.name: Shrine of Ranald
places.rules:
A Hero from the warband must visit the Gambling Den from Infamous Haunts. After rolling on the Gambling Chart he enters a shrine. Roll a D6:
1 Pickpocketed: lose 2D6 gold crowns
2-3 Find a Rabbit's Foot
4-5 Find a Lucky Charm
6 A dropped merchant's purse containing D6x10 gold crowns

places.name: Private Isle
places.rules:
Roll a D6 for each entry:
Oars (count as two clubs) Auto find
D3 cooking pots (count as helmets) Auto find
Corpse (still fresh) 2+
D6x5 gold crowns 3+
Map of Marienburg 4+
Rowing boat 5+
Roll on the Booty Chart 6+

places.name: Riverfront Inn
places.rules: The lookout spies a piece of freight caught in the river current. Roll on the Cargo Chart to see what type of freight is hauled out of the swell.

places.name: The Sickly Wood
places.rules: The spiteful trees hurl dead branches at the party: D6 Heroes in the warband receive D3 Strength 4 hits. Among the plant life of the Sickly Wood is a bulbous fungus, Boilswort, that bursts into a cloud of spores and bears the taint of Chaos. Any Hero who chooses to touch the fungus must roll on the Warp-touch Chart.

places.name: Fort Beg-Bribe
places.rules:
Roll a D6 to see if the Duc is running a campaign:
1 Beast Hunt! Each model in the warband must take a Toughness test. When D6 warriors have passed, the beast is slain, the bounty is claimed and no further tests are required. Roll on the Injury Charts for any model that fails its Toughness test. The bounty is D6 Treasures and the hide of the beast. Beast Hide gives its wearer a 6+ saving throw unmodified by Strength, and can be combined with other armour saves.
2-5 Inspection! Officials detain D6 members of the warband. Unless a donation of 50 gold crowns is paid, those warriors miss the first turn of the next battle.
6 Restock Supplies! Heroes receive a half-price discount on any equipment they find at the fort.

places.name: Wouduin Tollhouse
places.rules: Pay a toll of 1 gold crown for each model in your warband. A Highwayman or Road Warden Hired Sword joins the warband.

places.name: Rat Rock
places.rules:
If another player already owns Rat Rock, ignore the rest of this result: the discovering player may claim it through Scenario 5: Stockade as normal.
A banditti hide-out is concealed up in the crags, belonging to a trio of pyromaniac brigands. Roll a D6:
1-2 Booby Trap! The lair has been rigged with explosive charges. Resolve an exploding powder keg: all models in the warband that fail an Initiative test are within the blast range.
3-4 Lone Gunman! The warband is joined by a Pyromaniac Hired Sword from the Border Town Burning supplement.
5-6 Bandits! Three Heroes from your warband must pass Strength tests to overpower the bandits. Each Hero in the warband may attempt a Strength test until either three have passed or the attempt has failed. Any Hero rolling a 6 is injured: roll on the Serious Injury Chart and apply the result. If the bandits are overpowered the warband raids their arson stash.
After taking Rat Rock the warband may claim it as a fortified encampment. Rat Rock allows the owning player to play the False Beacons special scenario.
Roll a D6 for each entry:
Rope Auto find
Powder Keg 2+
Firecrackers 3+
Cathayan Candle/Firepot 4+
Herstel-Wenckler Pigeon Bombs 5+
Fire Bomb 6+

places.name: Laurelorn Forest
places.rules:
The warband leader must take a Leadership test to pass through the forest's faerie illusions. If the test is passed, the warband reaches the settlement unscathed, and the humans living in Laurelorn sell one each of the following at half price: Elf Bow, Elven Cloak, Elven Wine, Elven Boots, Blessed Stag Hide, Hunting Arrows.
If the test is failed the warband meets a troupe of glade guardians who block the path. Any dark elf Hired Swords with the warband are slain. If a Dark Elf or Goblin warband, or a warband following the 'Gaze of the Gods' plot, dares approach Laurelorn Forest it is attacked: each model in the warband must take a Toughness test, and if 2D6 warriors pass, the elves are driven off. Roll on the Injury Charts for any model that fails its Toughness test.

places.name: Ruins of Almshoven
places.rules:
The warband is joined by a Bard Hired Sword with his accursed instrument, typically a fiddle or a flute. He forms a 'Blood Pact' with the warband.
Unless they are following the 'Guarding the Peace' plot, warbands may choose to despoil the burial mounds while exploring the ruins: roll once on the Grave Robbery Chart for each Hero in the warband.

places.name: Cursed Village of Halsdorph
places.rules: Each Hero in the warband must take a Leadership test. Roll on the chart for the Dream Parlour from Infamous Haunts for any Hero who fails.

places.name: Mining Colony of Erlach
places.rules:
Roll a D6 for each entry:
Rope Auto find
D3 Pick-axes 2+
Powder Keg 3+
Pair of Mules 4+
Mine Cart (counts as a cart) 5+
Prospector Hired Sword 6+
If the old Prospector crosses your path he automatically forms a 'Blood Pact' with the warband.
A warband visiting Erlach may choose to play the special scenario: Colony of Plenty.

places.name: Pirate Town of Broekwater
places.rules:
Warbands involved in piracy can use the swampy retreat as a stopover: Pirate warbands or followers of Chaos search for rare items as normal in the post-battle sequence, and for any one rare item found, that item counts as the merchandise the Grey Mist gang was smuggling. The gang's stash holds multiple copies, so the Hero who found the item can buy an additional D3 of these items from the smugglers' stash.
Witch Hunters and other law enforcement warbands are refused entry by a well-equipped militia of angry locals.

places.name: Border Town of Aarnau
places.rules:
Human, elf and dwarf warbands are joined by one of the Wasteland Peacocks. The Aarnauen veteran counts as a Freelancer Hired Sword.
Other warbands get the chance to sack the town. For each Hero in the warband roll a D6:
1 The Hero is caught in the attempt by the town militia: roll on the Serious Injury Chart
2 Find 2D6 gold crowns
3 Steal a sacrificial goat
4 Capture one of the townsfolk as a hostage
5 Requisition a rowboat plus a fish-hook shot
6 Roll on the Cargo Chart, re-rolling a result of 1

places.name: Market Town of Klessen
places.rules:
Human, elf or dwarf warbands are joined by a Merchant Hired Sword with D3 bodyguards. If the warband already has a Merchant, he gains an outfit of D3 bodyguards.
Other warbands get the chance to ransack the market. For each Hero in the warband roll a D6:
1 The Hero is placed under arrest by the town's watch
2 Plunder a Treasure
3 Rustle a prize bull or a wild pig (counts as a War Boar)
4 Seize a villager as a captive
5 Hijack a hay wagon (counts as a Trade Wagon)
6 Pillage the town's armoury, which holds D6 hand weapons plus D6 handguns. If the dice result makes up a double, roll once on the Custom Weapons Chart.

places.name: Tannery
places.rules:
The Tannery on Tanners Alley is secretly a flesh house with links to a Cult of Slaanesh. The warband leader who finds it gains a random Chaos gift from the Graces of Shornaal (see the Corrupted Characters chapter) and the Tannery as an encampment.
The Tannery allows the owning warband to roll on the Tanner chart (result 4) within the leather goods table of Infamous Haunts.
Any warband following Drowning the Witch will instead burn the tannery to the ground and gain 150 gc.

places.name: Auction Hall
places.rules:
The Auction Hall can be used to sell any number of rare items, but once auctioned they must be sold regardless of the roll. Roll a D6 for each rare item being sold:
1-2 Half the item's base price
3-4 The item's full base price
5-6 The item's full price plus half
The Auction Hall counts as an encampment.

places.name: Trading Post
places.rules:
Searching the ruined trading post, the warband finds D3 swords, D3 helmets, D3 suits of light armour, D3 Cathayan Silk Cloaks and D3 Crossbow Pistols.
In addition, any warband may restore the trading post. A player does not have to decide immediately and may return between battles until another warband finds and restores it. The restoration costs D6x25+150 gold crowns and lasts four games in which at least one Hero and two henchmen must miss battles; each additional Hero or pair of henchmen helping speeds the rebuilding by one game, to a minimum of one.
A warband controlling the restored trading post rolls 3D6 to determine the experience of the henchmen available for hire after the battle, and gets +3 when searching for rare items. If the warband is following the 'Ten Great Families' plot, it gets +D6 campaign points once for rebuilding the trading post. The Trading Post counts as an encampment.

places.name: Lighthouse
places.rules:
The Lighthouse can be used if the warband has a boat. During the Trading phase of the post-battle sequence three Heroes may scavenge on the rock instead of searching for a rare item: make D3 rolls on the Cargo Chart to see what freight crashes onto the rocks.
The Lighthouse counts as an encampment. A dispute over a Lighthouse should be fought using Scenario 5: Stockade if boats can be used by the warbands to reach the island where it stands. The maximum number of models deployed in that scenario is how many models the boats can carry for each warband.

places.name: Laundrette
places.rules: The laundrette is a front for a drug lab and counts as an encampment. After every battle roll a D6 for drugs by referring to the Grave Robbery Chart in the post-battle sequence; one free dose of drugs is available. The warband may exchange a Cathayan Silk for D3 doses of the same drug, and as many doses can be taken as Cathayan Silks are exchanged.

places.name: Ship-of-the-Line
places.rules:
A ship-of-the-line is a small ship to be used in battles. The ship can be crewed by every model in a player's warband, including any cargo and objective markers.
If a second warband rolls the same result, they charter a ship from a pirate captain to contest the encampment. The dispute is settled in the next round by playing the special scenario: All Hands On Deck!

places.name: The Unterdock
places.rules: Your warband sets up a shady deal with one of the underfolk. Choose any item from the unknowable cargo list, the marketplace or Infamous Haunts. You may buy it from the Unterdock with no rarity roll, but the item costs its full price plus D6x25 gold crowns. The deal is for 1 item only and need not be redeemed immediately: any time you are able to buy equipment you may cash in the favour and buy the item.

places.name: Colony of the Lady's Tears
places.rules:
A warband arriving at the Shallyan refuge may choose to play the special scenario: Colony of Plenty, with the following changes.
Wandering Monsters are replaced with deadly fauna. Roll a D6 to find out what one of the warriors in your warband has encountered, determining the victim at random:
1-2 Boilswort. Dirty pink fungus on deformed trees releases spores tainted by Chaos and causes Neiglish Rot. The model becomes infected unless it passes a Toughness test. Undead models are not affected.
3-4 Blood Sedge. Man-eating plants native to the Cursed Marsh (see Carnivorous Plants, page 81 of the Border Town Burning supplement).
Replace 'Sleeping Monster', 'Bat Cave' and 'Powder Store' with 2D3 mutants: roll on the Random Mutation Chart to see what mutation applies to each group. 'Gold Rush' is replaced by Shallyan Serum. 'Greater Artefact' is replaced by the Divine Relic, the Blessed Instruments of Thaumaturgy, and its product, Shallyan Serum; these are treated exactly like Greater Artefacts for all purposes except plot requirements.
Blessed Instruments of Thaumaturgy: a set of consecrated alchemical implements used by the Shallyan church to harvest a gel from preserved bodies. They come with 1 dose of Shallyan Serum. Further doses may only be harvested from the bodies of dead priests: after any battle the warband holding the Blessed Instruments took part in, in which a priest died permanently, the warband gains 1 dose of Shallyan Serum.
Shallyan Serum heals any Hero of all previously suffered permanent injuries; strike all injuries from the Hero's profile. The serum may also raise a dead Hero, but only at the precise time of his death: if a Hero rolls 11-15 Dead, or is sacrificed, hanged or sold into slavery while the warband holds the serum, you may treat the result as Full Recovery and the warrior returns to the warband.

places.name: Hartshorn Lodge
places.rules:
A warband that discovers the Hartshorn Lodge may learn its darkest ritual. By paying D6 campaign points and 200 gold coins the Lodge teaches the warband how to create a Summoning Circle to bring forth Ark'il'hes, a Daemon Prince of Arkhar; the rules for using the circle and summoning the Prince are in the Dramatis Personae section.
If the warband follows either the 'Drowning the Witch' or 'Keeping the Peace' plot, or has no wizard, it may choose to burn the lodge to the ground and gain D3+1 campaign points.

places.name: Mist-wreathed Stronghold
places.rules:
D6 randomly determined models from the warband must pass an Initiative test or be dragged to their doom by the Fimir lurking in the mist. Remove any doomed models from the warband roster sheet.
If a Skaven or Beastmen warband or followers of Chaos survive the Fimir attack with their leader unscathed, they may claim the stronghold. The Mist-wreathed Stronghold counts as an encampment.
A Chaos warband that holds at least one Mutant Child realises one of the children's importance when it takes the stronghold: the child now counts as a hero with the stats of the warband's cheapest hero, immediately gains 10 Experience and all the level-ups that follow, and gains 2 random mutations. When the warband receives a mark of chaos the child receives the other mark (if the leader gains a mark of Arkhar the child receives the wizard mark; if the leader is a wizard the child receives the applicable warrior's mark).
If a Fimir warband reaches the stronghold a Young Noble may claim it as his lair. That Hero must become the warband leader, ascending to become a Noble: he gains 10 Experience points and counts as a large target.

places.name: Unseen Library
places.rules:
A warband that discovers the Unseen Library has several options. If the warband contains a wizard hero or hired sword, he may try to gain the knowledge in the books: if he passes a Leadership test you may deduct D3 campaign points and roll on the chart below.
1-2 The wizard learns 1 random chaos ritual
3-4 The wizard learns 1 random Necromancy spell
5-6 The wizard learns 1 random Ritual of Dhar
His education has begun: after each battle, instead of searching for an item or visiting a location, the wizard may return to the Unseen Library and learn another spell from the list he first rolled for. Once he has learnt every spell from that list he graduates to full membership and from then on gets +2 to every spell casting attempt.
If the warband follows either the 'Drowning the Witch' or 'Keeping the Peace' plot, or has no wizard, it may choose to destroy the library and gain D3+1 campaign points.

places.name: The Mouth of Morr
places.rules:
The Mouth of Morr can be used to ship rare items out of the city: a Hero can visit it in the post-battle sequence to sell any rare items at their full value.
If a warband is following 'The Secret Deal' plot, the Mouth of Morr can be used to smuggle any rare item that was being appropriated by the League of Gentlemen Entrepreneurs.
The Mouth of Morr can also be used to move hostages out of the city. If a warband is following 'The Body Trade' plot, it can transport captured models out of the city: two warriors, including at least one Hero, miss the next battle while transporting any number of captured models. For each captured model smuggled out this way, the number of hostage objective markers that must be moved through the Grand Sewer Network is reduced by one. When the player has accumulated 40 campaign points, if 12 captured warriors and stragglers have been sent through the Mouth of Morr the body trader is declared winner of the campaign.
If two or more warbands discover the Mouth of Morr then neither side can use it to transport.
